text:
marta: heads-up — p95 for /v1/generate jumped from ~220ms to ~820ms in the canary cohort after the runtime 2.4.0 rollout. no p99 spike yet but p95 is noisy. anyone seeing this?

devon: saw the same in cohort-7 around 11:12 UTC. short prompts (<=64 tokens) p95 up ~3.5x. dashboards show hotpath queueing and longer kernel init times.

alejandro: ops-bot alerted at 11:17. grabbing traces now. can you paste a couple of request ids so i can pull perftrace?

marta: sample ids: 2f8a9c, 2f8a9d, 2f8a9e. repro curl (canary header):
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Canary: 1" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"hi"}' https://canary.api.redwood/v1/generate
```

devon: kicking off synthetic replay against canary with seed=42. early look: kernel-selector picked "vector-kv" on several shards instead of fast-path. suspect selector heuristic change in 2.4.0.

sarah: ACME support ticket incoming — they've reported latency regressions and timed out clients. i'll prepare a customer-safe note once we have mitigation.

alejandro: pulled perftrace 98765 for req 2f8a9d. snippet:
```
hotpath_qdepth=12
worker_cpu_wait_ms=340
kernel_load_ms=78
auth_fetch_ms=110
```
queueing + auth fetch bump present on same node.

devon: quick mitigation option: route-level fallback to runtime v2.3 for affected tenant cohorts (set X-Runtime-Fallback header / routing rule). i'd rather do targeted rollback for the canary subgroup first.

marta: starting targeted rollback for cohort=canary-missing-kernel in 5m. we'll dark-launch (shadow) traffic to v2.3 and keep v2.4 running for analysis.

ops-bot: deploy rollback started — job 8675309 initiated by devon.

alejandro: noticed auth token fetch p95 increased ~120ms for some tenants in the same timeframe. unclear if causal or just correlated with queueing. collecting auth logs.

devon: repro steps for others to run locally:
1) set header X-Canary: 1
2) send 100 short prompt requests quickly
3) collect per-request kernel_name and latency_ms from /node/debug/requests
Command:
```
for i in {1..100}; do curl -s -H "X-Canary:1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://canary.api.redwood/v1/generate; done | jq -r '.latency_ms' | ./tools/stats
```
Also check /node/metrics for kernel_selector decisions.

marta: please also run synthetic replay with --oversubscribe 1.5 to surface queueing faster.

sarah: draft customer note: "we're investigating a latency regression impacting a small canary cohort. temporary routing fallback enabled for affected tenants. we'll share an update in 30 minutes." ok to send?
marta: send it.

devon: root cause hypothesis: 2.4.0 changed kernel selection heuristics (cpu_cpumask scoring) causing some node types to pick vector-kv path which has worse per-token latency for short prompts due to cache alignment. repro on c5g-large variant.

alejandro: bisect plan: introduce a feature flag to disable the new selector, roll to 10% of canary, measure p95, then 50%/100%. if p95 improves we keep the flag off and ship a patch.

ops-bot: rollback job 8675309 completed: cohort "canary-missing-kernel" scaled back to v2.3. monitoring.

devon: post-rollback p95 in that cohort dropped back to ~240ms. leaving rollback in place until we have safe selector toggle and synthetic tests.

sarah: i've updated ACME with the incident link and that a rollback is in place.

alejandro: follow-ups: add a short-prompt synthetic suite to CI, expose kernel-selector telemetry per request, and add an A/B flag for selector so future rollouts can be toggled without full rollback.

marta: filing INC-2026 and will author the postmortem once bisect completes. thanks team. :thumbsup:
